text:
Shane Pinto is the center Ottawa sends out for 20 minutes a night, and lately he has been the one deciding games. His go-ahead goal beat Calgary on Nov. 23 and stretched the Senators' point streak to nine, and that same week Jake Sanderson told TSN a Pinto fight "got the bench rocking." Among every skater in the league, only 19 have added more wins with their goals by our count.

Ten goals and 18 points in 27 games, and the scoring looks honest. Ten goals on 10.2 expected, his own chances steady at 1.11 expected goals per 60 minutes, and his points pace sits in the middle of our talent range. Over the last ten games his chances have actually climbed, 4.8 expected goals against a usual 3.8, which is the trend you want to see.

The part to watch is defensive. Ottawa's share of the chances at five on five is more than five points worse with him on the ice than without him, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers. He scores like a top-six center. The two-way piece is still catching up.
